leads.title: Nerves traced to the brain by dissection in Ptolemaic Alexandria
leads.why: Human dissection distinguished nerves from tendons and vessels, separated sensory from motor nerves and tied both to the brain, the account that Galen extended and medicine kept.
leads.verify: The works of Herophilus and Erasistratus are lost; establish what later sources securely attribute to them. Note earlier claims that the brain is the seat of the senses (Alcmaeon; the Edwin Smith papyrus) and Galen's experiments (c. 170 CE). This overlaps with anatomy by dissection under health.

leads.title: Animal electricity found in nerve and muscle in Bologna
leads.why: Frog-leg experiments showed that nerves carry an electrical signal, founding electrophysiology, and the dispute over them led Volta to the battery.
leads.verify: Date the experiments and the 1791 De viribus electricitatis, and the Galvani-Volta dispute. Record the measurement of the nerve signal by du Bois-Reymond and Helmholtz (1840s-1850) and its ionic explanation (1952) as later records.

leads.title: Microbes shown to cause fermentation and decay in France
leads.why: Showing that microbes cause fermentation and do not arise spontaneously founded microbiology, and led to pasteurisation, antisepsis and the germ theory of disease.
leads.verify: Date Pasteur's lactic fermentation memoir (1857), the swan-neck flask experiments (1859-62) and the heating of wine (1864). Record the earlier findings of Cagniard-Latour, Schwann and Kutzing (1837) that yeast is alive, and Spallanzani on spontaneous generation.

leads.title: Induced pluripotent stem cells in Kyoto
leads.why: Four genes sufficed to return skin cells to an embryonic state, giving patient-specific cells for disease models, drug testing and transplantation without embryos.
leads.verify: Date the mouse (2006) and human (2007) papers and the parallel human work in Wisconsin. Record Gurdon's nuclear transfer in frogs (1962) and embryonic stem cells (1981, 1998) as what it built on.

leads.title: Weaver ants used to protect citrus in southern China
leads.why: Growers bought and placed ant nests in citrus trees to keep down pests, the oldest recorded deliberate use of one species to control another, and one still practised.
leads.verify: The date rests on the Nanfang caomu zhuang, whose attribution to 304 CE is disputed; give the earliest secure text (ninth-century sources are safer). This sits on the border with crop husbandry and may be better placed there.

leads.title: Extinction and the succession of fossil faunas established in Paris
leads.why: Comparative anatomy proved that mammoths and giant sloths belonged to vanished species, giving life a history and palaeontology its method.
leads.verify: Date Cuvier's 1796 papers on elephants and Megatherium and the Paris Basin work with Brongniart (1808-11). Record William Smith's use of fossils to order strata in England (1799-1815) as a parallel line that may merit its own record.

concepts.name: The electrical nature of nerve and muscle action
concepts.summary: Knowing that nerves and muscles work by electricity generated in the living tissue.

concepts.name: Biological pest control
concepts.summary: Protecting a crop by deliberately establishing the natural enemies of its pests.

concepts.name: The brain and nerves as the organ of sensation and movement
concepts.summary: Knowing that sensation, movement and thought depend on the brain and on nerves running to and from it.

concepts.name: Reprogramming cells to a pluripotent state
concepts.summary: Turning a specialised adult cell back into a cell that can form any tissue.

concepts.name: Extinction and the succession of life
concepts.summary: Knowing that species have died out and that different assemblages of living things have followed one another through time.

concepts.name: Microbes as the agents of fermentation and decay
concepts.summary: Knowing that fermentation and putrefaction are the work of living micro-organisms, which arise only from other micro-organisms.
